subject: Request: Art. 30 excerpt + subprocessor KMS access justification
messages:
From: procurement@northbridge-fin.com
To: chloe.martin@redwood.com
Cc: security@northbridge-fin.com
Date: 2026-07-29T09:31:00Z
Subject: Evidence request: Art.30 excerpt & KMS/subprocessor access justification

Hi Chloe,

We're progressing through procurement and require a concise extract of Article 30 (processing activities) that maps Redwood's role and the list of subprocessors touching personal data for processing in the EU environment. In particular Security has flagged the need for: 
- an excerpt that describes data categories and processing purposes as they relate to the NorthBridge integration (PII + transaction metadata),
- a short justification and access model for any subprocessor KMS access (who/why/how long),
- a current key-rotation and split-key plan or diagram for keys used to protect customer data at rest.

Can you provide an Art.30 excerpt + a customer-facing KMS access justification document by EOD tomorrow? Security prefers something we can attach to the DPA addendum rather than internal architecture diagrams. If anything is sensitive we can accept a redacted extract and a separate ops diagram.

Also: if Redwood needs to provide DPIA support or a short ops walk-through for our GDPR team, please advise availability next week (UTC+1).

Thanks,
Eleni Papadopoulos
Procurement 
NorthBridge Financial
attachments: none
From: chloe.martin@redwood.com
To: procurement@northbridge-fin.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, security@northbridge-fin.com
Date: 2026-07-29T13:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Evidence request: Art.30 excerpt & KMS/subprocessor access justification

Hi Eleni — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Lauren from Legal (cc) and Marissa from Privacy Ops to scope what we can publish customer-facing.

Short summary of what we will provide by COB tomorrow (redacted, customer-facing):
1) Art.30 excerpt (PDF): single-page register excerpt showing processing categories and high-level purposes for hosted inference and embeddings when integrated via API.
2) Subprocessor KMS access justification (PDF): for each subprocessor that operates systems with access to encrypted customer artifacts (e.g., blob storage, backups), we will provide: subprocessor name, role, limited access reason, scope (read-only / key-wrapping / key-management), and retention/expiry for temporary access.
3) KMS key hierarchy diagram (PNG): high-level, ops view showing key ownership (customer vs. Redwood root keys) — we will redact ticket IDs and internal hostnames.

Two clarifications we need from you to tailor the materials: 
- Are you accepting a redacted KMS diagram plus a short signed letter that confirms Redwood does not grant cross-customer key access? Or do you need the full key-id list for the keys used in your tenant?
- Is the DPIA support limited to a slide-deck and 60-minute session with your GDPR reviewer, or do you expect hands-on evidence collection for your internal DPIA?

We will attach the redacted Art.30 excerpt and the justification PDF to the email when submitting. If you confirm the level of detail for the KMS list, we can include the appropriate level of detail.

Regards,
Chloe Martin
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_art30_excerpt_redacted.pdf, kms-key-hierarchy-diagram.png
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
To: chloe.martin@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, procurement@northbridge-fin.com, security@northbridge-fin.com
Date: 2026-07-29T16:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Evidence request: Art.30 excerpt & KMS/subprocessor access justification

Chloe / Marissa — drafting notes and internal position. Please treat as internal until we sign-off the customer-facing versions.

1) Art.30: prepare a one-page excerpt limited to: controller/processor designation, documented categories of data processed for API/embedded workloads, processing purposes (inference, logging for reliability, billing metrics), and references to retention periods. Avoid internal pipeline names.

2) Subprocessor KMS access: we will categorize access into three buckets: 
   - Administrative (Redwood-managed key vaults; no plaintext exported);
   - Emergency, time-boxed access (for incident response; logged and approved via runbook ticket);
   - Technical integration (cloud provider-managed key ops for disk encryption).
Include a sentence confirming that Redwood does not grant subprocessors permanent, cross-customer key access and that any emergency access requires approval and rotation.

3) Art. 30 vs. DPA addendum: Procurement asked for a signed statement suitable for the DPA addendum. I can provide a short (three paragraph) attest letter on company letterhead that confirms the excerpt maps to our Article 30 register and that the listed subprocessors have controlled, limited access. We will not enumerate internal key IDs in the letter.

4) DPIA support: Marissa, can we offer a 45–60 minute call with a 6-slide deck and an ops Q&A? If they require CLI-level evidence (key IDs, audit log exports), we should route that to Dedicated/Private onboarding under an access request and appropriate NDAs.

Marissa: please prepare the customer-facing PDF drafts (redacted) and the ops slide-deck. Chloe: I recommend the letter be ready to sign by Legal once we confirm NBF's scope.

Thanks — L.
From: procurement@northbridge-fin.com
To: chloe.martin@redwood.com
Cc: security@northbridge-fin.com
Date: 2026-07-30T15:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Evidence request: Art.30 excerpt & KMS/subprocessor access justification

Thanks Chloe / Lauren — that plan works. A few quick replies: 
- We accept a redacted diagram plus the attest letter for the DPA addendum. We do not need full key-id lists in the letter, but Security will request key ids and signed audit-log extracts if we move to a production Dedicated deployment (that will be handled in the onboarding pipeline).
- DPIA support: a 60-minute live session with slides and a short Q&A is sufficient for our initial review. If follow-ups are needed, we'll open a separate evidence request.

Could you send the redacted Art.30 excerpt and the KMS justification PDF by EOD tomorrow (UTC+1)? Also propose two times for the DPIA session next week (we prefer mornings).

Best,
Eleni Papadopoulos
Procurement
NorthBridge Financial
attachments: none
